title: Eddie Palmieri and Rene Hernandez's arrangements
summary: He criticizes Palmieri's Columbia album and credits Hernandez.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Tell me about -- what do you think about some of Eddie recent experiments?

That's another guy with the same problem, the same identical problem. They ain't got no label because they don't produce no label. They want to reach the roof but they ain't go no ladder to get over there.
That was a beautiful thing. And I was the first guy -- when I heard that, I said, this is it. And right away, that's when I recorded my (unintelligible) with
Dizzy Gillespie. I said, this is the right moment, because this guy is coming with this, he going to make a explosion, and let me follow through with something.
But everything he played after that is the same thing.

And all the arrangements Rene made for the album for Columbia, he came here, they couldn't get no (unintelligible) they couldn't record it. They went back to Puerto Rico and they got to go after a three-day in the studio and the week after Rene died. So they didn't record none of that. Why? Because every time they -- Eddie sit down at a piano to play that, he find faults with the orchestra. (Unintelligible.)
Of course, Rene Alandos had a lot to do with Benito, didn't he?
Well, that was the first album they made.

Between him and , they made a album. You go back to the same identical thing. All those arrangements of bass parts was created by Rene. This guy did very little in there. He took a team, he almost spent five minutes, tried to dilute the thing in the piano all by himself before the bass coming in, and to me, up to now, he didn't dilute the thing yet.

When you hear a piano like this kid now, Chico Ria, and about a half a dozen outstanding piano players today, you ain't going to put that guy in that class today, because when they run a scale, they (unintelligible.) But even so, Eddie (unintelligible) but he ain't got it nohow. So now he brought (unintelligible) and the conga from California. He spent a whole lot of money, but he don't know how to marry one thing with the other. Why? Because (unintelligible). And then he wants to __________ everything, on top of that.

So to me, he be coming too (unintelligible) the music. And he's lucky that the Columbians spend a whole lot of money, and he B.S., with the result -- the album is out, the results in the album -- I advise everybody to buy the album, sit down home and listen, and tell me what you're listening to there. Because I be listening and I can't get no head and tail. Maybe I'm wrong. If I'm wrong, I'm willing to admit it.
